hero.title: Give to grow, grow to give more.
hero.lead: We connect generosity with need in a strategic, sustainable way. We do not replace foundations, we amplify them. And here, those who give also grow.
model.t: The social sector is fragmented. We are the bridge.
model.p: We strengthen foundations in the field, connect donors with verified causes and build an ecosystem where giving brings real benefits to those who contribute.
feat.hub.p: An operations center. Five routes linking alliances, donations and measurable impact.
feat.grat.p: A network of partner businesses offering exclusive discounts to every active member.
feat.tax.p: A 25% discount on income tax owed (Art. 257 ET) for each donation made through the financial system, under the terms and limits set by law.

traz.3.p: We match the specific need with the right donor.

origen.t: It all began with a ton of food.
origen.p1: After weeks of work, a campaign hit its goal: a ton of food to deliver to a foundation. But on arrival, the foundation had no way to store or distribute it all. Nearly half was lost. Watching that food go to waste —food someone needed just blocks away— left the founder with a question that wouldn’t let go: how do I close the gap between resources and need, with what I have at hand?
origen.p2: That question became a method. Give&Grow International grew out of nearly four years of Juan Sebastián Navarro Osorio’s field work in La Guajira, the Sierra Nevada and the comunas of Medellín, and was constituted by private document on April 11, 2025, registered with the Medellín Chamber of Commerce on May 19, 2025, as a nonprofit (ESAL) under the Special Tax Regime. The purpose: to restore trust in the act of giving, with traceability and no opaque intermediaries.
hub.lead: The operations center where alliances, donations and impact meet.
hub.r1.p: We strengthen verified foundations with logistics and visibility, without replacing their work. Real example: Fundación Niños del Futuro, in Manrique (Medellín), with Chefs del Futuro and Borboletas.
hub.r2.p: In-kind and monetary donations with full traceability: record, photo and report. Real example: at NDF a plate of food costs $4,000 COP and your gift turns into plates delivered, with evidence.
hub.r3.p: Strengthening the capacities of the partner foundations themselves: that line is still being built. The training that already happens in the network is theirs — our role is to channel resources, document it and give it visibility.
hub.form.p: Give&Grow does not dictate these programmes: they are designed and sustained by the partner foundations, who know their people. Our role is to channel resources, document what happens and give it visibility. The credit and the merit are theirs.
hub.form.mira: They all share something with MIRA: they do not stop at teaching a technique. They aim for the person to discover that they are capable — and that is what widens their gaze on their own future.
hub.r4.p: Experiences that take donors and partner teams to the field, with real communities and an impact report. We have run the first journeys with donors and partners; we are deepening the model before opening it to company teams.
hub.r5.p: A bridge to employment for vulnerable populations. Future phase. Example: 12 to 18 months of support for a person leaving incarceration, connected to training (R3) and to the partner companies in the network.
hub.pob.t: The populations we aim to reach
hub.pob.list: Children at risk - Indigenous communities - Rural communities - People living on the street - Older adults - Abused animals - People in rehabilitation - Incarcerated people

nav.d.voluntariado: How to take part in the field, in three levels
vol.lead: We want whoever arrives to widen their gaze, and the foundation to end up with something it did not have before. Both things, in the same day.
vol.niv.t: There are three ways to be here
vol.niv.p: Your profession does not define the level: setting foot in the territory does. You can contribute only from the structure, only in the field, or split your time between both.
vol.n1.p: In the field, alongside a partner foundation and its team. They know their community: they decide when a visit helps and which spaces are shared.
vol.n2.p: Your craft strengthens the structure that holds the network — law, accounting, development, design, training. It happens outside the territory.
vol.n3.p: You combine both, in whatever proportion you choose. A web designer who works on the site and also joins a field day; someone in communications who documents what happens.
vol.mira.p: We call it MIRA because that is what it is about: widening the gaze. And because the acronym names its four phases — Marco (Frame), Inmersión (Immersion), Reflexión (Reflection) and Anclaje (Anchoring).
vol.mira.obj: Its technical name states it precisely: a methodology for widening the perceptual field through significant experiences.
vol.mira.def.p: The perceptual field is everything a person manages to see as possible — for themselves and for their surroundings. When someone grows up believing certain things are “not for them”, that limit is often not one of ability: it is one of perception. And the same happens on the other side: someone who has never been in a neighbourhood cannot see what already works there.
vol.mira.def.p2: MIRA works right there. It does not give a speech: it designs an experience where the person does something they did not believe possible, and then helps them put it into words. What widens is not the information they hold: it is what they manage to see as possible.
vol.mira.sigla.t: The four phases, letter by letter
vol.f1.q: It opens the field. A field on the defensive admits no new perception: first a safe space is agreed and a challenge that breaks expectation is set.
vol.f2.q: It creates tension. The experience introduces something the current field cannot explain. That discomfort is what forces it to widen — which is why the challenge must be demanding, though reachable.
vol.f3.q: It consolidates. Lived experience becomes perception when it is put into words. Without this phase the experience fades and the field closes again.
vol.f4.q: It anchors. A small, achievable commitment carries the widened gaze into everyday life, so it does not stay in the day that passed.
vol.mira.why.p: Because removing any of them breaks the chain. Without Frame there is no openness. Without Immersion there is nothing new to explain. Without Reflection there is no meaning, only an anecdote. And without Anchoring there is no transfer: the day stays in the day. That is what separates MIRA from a nice field trip.
vol.mira.teo: It is not a new idea: it draws on the psychology of the perceptual field (Combs and Snygg), Bandura's self-efficacy and Kolb's experiential learning cycle. What is ours is applying it both ways.
vol.f1.v: You come to learn from someone who knows something you don't.
vol.f1.p: "You are going to solve something you had never tried."
vol.f2.p: A leading role in the challenge, not a spectator's seat.
vol.f3.v: "What did I believe before arriving that I no longer believe?"
vol.f3.p: "What did I discover in myself that I didn't know I had?"
vol.f4.v: What you are going to give back.
vol.f4.p: A small commitment in their own surroundings.
vol.mira.cierre: Two gazes that widen towards each other. That is giving to grow, and growing to give more.
vol.cuid.p: We work with children and young people. That is why care is not a clause at the end: it is in the design.
vol.cuid.1: Two verifications before setting foot in the field: ours and that of the foundation accompanying that community.
vol.cuid.2: Never alone: every activity happens accompanied by the foundation's team.
vol.cuid.3: Consent comes before the camera. Photos are decided by the foundation and the families, never by the visitor.
vol.cuid.4: If the foundation feels it is not the right moment, we wait. The community sets the pace.
vol.port.p: A single agreement with Give&Grow opens several different experiences. No single foundation can offer that.
vol.port.note: This is how the model is designed. Each experience opens when there is a verified partner foundation for that population — and the network grows one alliance at a time.
vol.hoy.p: We have run the first journeys with donors and partners. With company teams we are opening the format: if your team wants to be the first, let's talk. None of this is charged for.

faq.q11: My home was damaged by the earthquake. What do you do?
faq.a11: If the danger is happening NOW — a wall about to fall, a smell of gas, someone trapped — call 123 and your local council: that does not wait. For everything else there is Mira Mi Casa: you upload photos of your home and a licensed volunteer engineer gives you an opinion at a distance, free of charge. They tell you whether there are signs not to stay in the house or in part of it, what precautions to take meanwhile, and which materials to repair it with and in what order.
faq.q12: Will you tell me whether my home is safe to live in?
faq.a12: No, and it is worth knowing why. Photos do not show the foundations, or the ground, or whether that crack is in a load-bearing wall. And the ruling that carries legal effects — evacuate, demolish — belongs to your municipal authority and not to a private party: Colombia's Law 1523 of 2012 sets that. What we do give you is an opinion on what the photos allow us to see. And if we recommend not using part of the house while it is being checked, that is a precaution, not a ruling of uninhabitability.
faq.q13: Will you repair my house or give me the materials?
faq.a13: We cannot commit to that house by house, and we would rather say so than promise something that does not depend on us alone. As a foundation we will try to arrange help for as many homes as we can. What you do receive for certain is the opinion: which materials to repair with and in what order, so you know where to start even if you source them yourself.
faq.a14: There is no date, and promising one would be worse. The engineers are volunteers and the most serious cases are looked at first. What we do give you are two verifiable figures on your link: how many days you have been waiting and how many cases are still unopened. Keep that link: it is where you see how your case is going and where you upload more photos if we ask for them.
faq.q15: I am an engineer. How can I help?
faq.a15: You apply on the “Volunteer engineers” page with your COPNIA licence number. We check it against COPNIA's public register and access is granted by hand, so it is not instant. What you will do is give an opinion at a distance based on photos — staying, precautions, materials and visit priority — never a habitability ruling. You do not see the family's contact details or address: they are not needed to give the opinion.
faq.q1: How do I make a donation?
faq.a1: In the calculator you pick your amount and continue to payment: you pay by card or with the Bancolombia Button through Wompi, Bancolombia's gateway, and come back with your tracking number. If you prefer a bank transfer, the Bancolombia savings account is 31000009221 in the name of Fundación Give&Grow International (NIT 901.948.930-2); report it afterwards on the site: you get your tracking number instantly and upload your proof right there. That beats emailing it, because your gift is registered and traceable from the first minute.
faq.a2: A network of partner businesses offering exclusive discounts to every active member, from the Sprout tier. Businesses gain visibility as purpose-driven, and members access benefits at partner businesses as they join.
faq.q3: How does the tax benefit work?
faq.a3: For every donation made through the financial system you get a 25% credit against income tax payable (Art. 257 of the Colombian Tax Code), within the cap set by Art. 258. For example, COP 4,000,000 donated may mean up to COP 1,000,000 less tax, depending on your tax situation. We are not tax advisers: confirm it with your accountant.
faq.a4: Yes. You can contribute from your own craft — health, law, accounting, communications, development, teaching and more — in the field alongside a partner foundation, in the Hub's structure, or combining both. Tell us your area and your availability.
faq.q5: Can my foundation apply to the Hub?
faq.a5: Yes. We look for legally constituted foundations with verifiable field work and a willingness to embrace traceability. Some partners contribute services to the Hub instead of only receiving.
faq.q6: What makes the Social Hub unique?
grat.cats.note: We are onboarding partner businesses; these are the categories we prioritize. Specific benefits are announced as they are confirmed.
faq.q7: Can I make a one-time gift instead of monthly?
faq.a7: Yes. In the calculator you can choose One-off for a single gift, or Monthly/Annual for a recurring one. In every case you receive your receipt with a tracking number once the payment is confirmed. The donation certificate for tax purposes is separate: you request it when you give, it is signed by the Legal Representative and the Statutory Auditor under oath, and a person issues it — which is why we need your ID document and your city.
faq.a8: Yes. For international donors we enable PayPal; write to us and we will share the link. Note that the Art. 257 ET deduction applies to income-tax payers in Colombia.
faq.q9: How do I know where my gift went?
faq.a9: Evidence, not promises. Every gift follows our traceability: a receipt with a tracking number once the payment is confirmed, a delivery record signed by whoever receives it, and its photos published in your gift's tracking page. If you requested a donation certificate, it is issued reviewed and signed. We tell you where it went and who it helped.
faq.a10: ImpactOS is the system we use to bring traceability and visibility to the Hub impact. ALMA is the assistant that answers your questions about the foundation here on the site. Both are under construction and grow with the network.

faq.a6: The HUB SOCIAL is not just a channel for giving: it is an operations centre with five routes connecting partnerships, donations and measurable impact. Three things set us apart. First, real traceability: your gift has a tracking number, an automatic receipt, a signed donation certificate and a handover record with photos you can see in the tracking page. Second, evidence rather than promises: we are a young, transparent foundation that shows what it can prove, with no inflated figures, and we work with partner foundations verified on the ground. Third, reciprocity: whoever gives also grows — members access the Gratitude Program benefits and companies gain visibility as businesses with purpose. That is what our motto sums up: «Give to grow, grow to give more».

impactos.t: ImpactOS: the record behind every gift.
impactos.lead: Not a future promise. It is the layer that turns an intention to give into a record with a destination, evidence and a certificate — and it is already running on this site.
impactos.why.p: The sector's problem is not a lack of generosity: it is that almost no one keeps the record. Without a system, every donation is a one-off favour — impossible to audit, to repeat or to report precisely. ImpactOS exists so that giving no longer depends on someone's memory.
impactos.os.p: The layer that brings together in one place the record of the network, the impact calculation, field traceability and certificates. In Spanish it sounds like impactos; in English it stands for Impact Operating System.
impactos.using.p: No need to imagine it. Almost everything you saw on this site comes from ImpactOS:
impactos.u1.p: The map and the wall of partner foundations are drawn from a single verified source: who joined, which area they work in, and with what consent their material is published.
impactos.u2.p: The calculator does not guess: it uses units documented by the foundations themselves. A plate of food at Niños del Futuro costs $4,000 COP, and that is where the equivalence you see comes from.
impactos.u3.t: The destination, from the first click
impactos.u3.p: When you go to donate from a foundation's profile, the record is born directed to it. It is not a field someone fills in later: it is in the gift from the start.
impactos.u4.p: The interface that answers in plain language about the network, memberships and the tax benefit, reading the same verified data.
impactos.rec.p: This is what ImpactOS keeps about a donation. You build the first part with the site; the Social Hub produces the second on the ground.

impactos.rec.b: What the Hub produces on the ground

impactos.rec.r7.v: With a photo of what was received
impactos.rec.r8.v: Signed by the person who receives

impactos.jor.p: The record is not only about donations. A volunteering journey leaves its own trail, with the same structure: what is agreed before setting foot on the ground, and what stays documented at the close.

impactos.jor.r3.v: With the HUB, with Give&Grow, or mixed
impactos.jor.note: It is the same principle as the record of a donation: if it was not documented, it did not happen.
impactos.jor.link: How we measure what happens there
med.lead: The work on the ground belongs to the partner foundation; we amplify it, record it and report it. This page states the evidence we speak from — and where what we can prove ends.
med.contrib.p: Give&Grow does not cause the impact on its own: the foundation does the work in its community. That is why every report is written in terms of contribution. It is the technically correct way, and it is what the motto already says: we do not replace foundations, we amplify them.
med.contrib.yv: Your gift contributed to the foundation delivering N meals, with a record and a photo.
med.contrib.note: The difference looks like wording and it is not: in the first sentence the credit stays where the work was done, and the contribution stays verifiable.
med.esc.p: Measuring impact has degrees, and confusing them is the most common mistake in the sector. These are the three, with the real status of each.
med.e1.p: What one real unit of service costs, documented by the foundation that provides it. A meal at Niños del Futuro costs $4,000 COP, and that is where the equivalence in the calculator comes from. It measures what was delivered.
med.e2.p: What changed in people, beyond what was delivered. The MIRA instruments record it in aggregated, anonymous form. Without a professional on the team we observe, we do not diagnose: we issue no individual results and no clinical conclusions.
med.e3.p: We do not publish it, and this is not decorative caution: an SROI is not a calculation, it is a study. It requires financial proxies, a baseline, consultation with stakeholders, and four technical discounts — deadweight, attribution, displacement and drop-off. Without those, a social return ratio falls apart in the first meeting, and everything else that is true falls with it.
med.esc.note: The first rung measures what was delivered; the third would measure the value of the change produced. They are not the same thing. The raw material already exists: ImpactOS records destination, unit, receipt, delivery and report. What is missing is the outcomes layer and the methodological rigour, not the data.
med.pub.p: These rules govern every figure on this site and in any report we sign.
med.pub.1: Always aggregated and anonymous: never an identifiable individual case.
med.pub.2: With recorded consent for any material from the community — photo, testimony or journal.
med.pub.3: With a visible cut-off date: a figure without a date is not evidence.
med.pub.4: With the source stated: which instrument produced it, whether a record, a journey log or an observation.
med.pub.5: Third-party figures are marked as reported, never as our own.
med.pub.6: We prefer recency over cumulative totals: how many journeys and how long ago the last evidence was says more than an unaudited total.
med.pub.7: No social return ratios as long as there is no study to support them.
med.rep.t: The report for the partner company
med.rep.p: When a team takes part in a journey, this is what it receives. The structure is the real one; the fields are filled with what that journey actually produced, and nothing more.
med.rep.meta: With cut-off date and record number
med.rep.g1a: Activity carried out, with an active role for the community
med.rep.g1b: Participants from the company and effective hours
med.rep.g3: What was observed · aggregated and anonymous
med.rep.g3a: In the company team: synthesis of the closing reflection
med.rep.g3b: In the participants: aggregated synthesis of the observation
med.rep.g4b: Photographic evidence, according to the consent granted
med.rep.note: Every report includes its methodological note: it describes the contribution of the journey, the work on the ground belongs to the partner foundation, and it does not constitute a social return calculation.
med.map.t: How it translates into the frameworks your company already uses
med.map.p: No company is going to adopt a new framework: it already reports under the SDGs, GRI or ESG. That is why our core set of indicators comes with a translation layer.
med.map.note: The mapping is offered as a reference so the company can integrate ours into its own report. We do not audit that report, nor do we certify its compliance.
med.unlock.t: The second rung does not need a budget
med.unlock.p: It needs a professional. A volunteer psychologist could validate the observation instruments and define how far we can claim without over-interpreting. The volunteering programme already has the channel to receive one, without setting foot on the ground if they prefer.

vis.t: Make giving transparent, measurable and mutual.
vis.p: Our goal is to build Colombia's most trusted social-impact network: every gift transforming a life with full traceability and, in doing so, helping the giver grow too. We start in Medellín; the horizon is Latin America.
vis.1.p: Every donation with a destination, evidence and a measurable result, not promises.
vis.2.p: Amplify those already working in the field, cutting costs and multiplying their reach.
vis.3.p: A model where giving leaves a real mark and, at the same time, benefits the giver.
membres.lead: Becoming a member means giving regularly and growing with the foundation. Each tier adds benefits on top of the previous one, with suggested amounts and the option to give another value.

brig.t: The 10 August earthquake. Five territories, 24–28 August.
brig.lead: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake with its epicentre in Chocó struck the west of the country. From 24 to 28 August we deliver in five territories, alongside the foundations already working in each one. Until the 24th there are four ways to help, and none is worth less than the others.
brig.hechos.nota: Casualty and displacement figures change by the hour and are published by the national risk agency (UNGRD). We do not repeat them here: it would mean publishing a number that is false tomorrow.
brig.plan.ey: What we are going to do
brig.plan.t: Seven people, five sectors, more than a hundred families in each.
brig.plan.p: Collection happens at drop-off points hosted by companies and friends. From there the load leaves with the team, by road, on 24 August.
brig.sec.nota: Exact areas and delivery points are set with each city's Municipal Risk Management Council and with the partner foundation in that territory. Quantities are calculated for 100 families per sector and are adjusted against the official needs list before purchasing.
brig.hub.t: We do not show up to hand things out on our own.
brig.hub.p: We deliver alongside foundations that already work in each territory and know the families: they bring the judgement and the relationship, we bring the logistics, the supplies and the record. It is the same HUB model we run all year, applied to an emergency.
brig.nec.p: The full inventory has more than a hundred items across thirteen categories, twenty-four of them critical. This is what they group, and why.
brig.c1.r: Without a lid, water is recontaminated within hours.
brig.c1.d: Purification tablets, sealed buckets, gravity filters and waste management.
brig.c2.r: Pull-tab cans are mandatory: in an emergency there is no can opener.
brig.c2.d: Canned protein, ready-to-eat pulses, oral rehydration salts and disposable tableware.
brig.c3.r: There are intimate needs nobody asks for out loud.
brig.c3.d: Soap, toilet paper, complete menstrual hygiene kits and new underwear.
brig.c4.r: Always forgotten, and their absence humiliates.
brig.c4.d: Early childhood and older adults: nappies by size, wipes and barrier cream.
brig.c5.r: Sleeping on a sports hall floor is the number one complaint.
brig.c5.d: Insulating mats, mountain-weather blankets, waterproof tarpaulins and ponchos.
brig.c6.r: Talking to your family is not a luxury: it is a humanitarian need.
brig.c6.d: Solar lamps, torches, batteries and power strips that turn one socket into a community charging point.
brig.c7.r: The brigade never consumes what belongs to the families.
brig.c7.d: Helmets, boots, certified masks, institutional ID and the handover records.

hub.intro.p1: A Hub is a meeting point: a place where people, resources and capabilities that would otherwise never meet get connected. It does not replace those already doing the work; it links them so their effort reaches further.
hub.intro.t2: So, what is Give&Grow's Social Hub?
hub.intro.p2: It is our on-the-ground engine: the bridge connecting the generosity of donors and companies with verified grassroots foundations, in a traceable and sustainable way. Here, those who give also grow, and every contribution arrives with evidence: records, photos and invoices.
hub.found.t: Who makes up the network today
hub.found.p: We begin with one partner foundation and a network in the process of formal onboarding. Each one joins one at a time, with verification and an agreement — no inflated names or figures.

brig.est.p: Everything that arrives before the 24th travels with the brigade. What arrives later goes to the next journey — it is not returned and it is not lost.
brig.est.p.despues: Every delivery is published here with its signed record. What arrives now goes to the next journey.
brig.nec4.cap: Four ways to help, and all of them are needed
brig.n1.d: It is what lets us buy what is actually missing, in the size and format that works. Bank transfer, or online: online you come back with a tracking number and can follow your gift all the way to the record signed by whoever receives it.
brig.n2.d: Write to us before buying. It sounds like red tape and it is the opposite: we tell you what is missing today, so your money does not end up in something that cannot be delivered.
brig.n3.d: In Envigado there are boxes someone has to receive, check and pack. No experience needed, and not a whole day either: what is needed is showing up.
brig.n4.d: If you cannot give, you can open a door: a warehouse, a truck heading to the coffee region, a company willing to lend its premises. One message from you to the right person moves as much as a donation.
brig.mc.t: Hands and contacts are needed too.
brig.mc.p: Not everything is solved with money. Two things we need that almost nobody offers, because almost nobody asks for them.
brig.mc.manos.p: The travelling team is already closed at seven people: going into the field requires two vettings — ours and the local foundation's — plus a Marco session, and that does not fit in the days left. What we do need is people in Envigado to receive, sort and pack what arrives at the drop-off points. In the form, choose «With Give&Grow — in the structure».
brig.mc.cont.p: The most useful thing you can send us if you are not going to donate, and it costs nothing: a warehouse or car park in Envigado or nearby where we can sort; a truck or van heading to Cali, Pereira, Manizales, Armenia or Chocó between the 24th and the 28th; a company willing to lend its premises as a drop-off point; or a foundation already working in one of the five territories.
vf.origen.brig: You came from the earthquake brigade. We ticked «in the structure» because that is what can be joined in time: the Medellín drop-off point, 24–28 August. You can change it if you would rather join the year-round programme.

brig.dar.especie.a1.dir: Carrera 48 # 37 Sur 56, opposite the Viva Envigado roundabout
brig.dar.especie.aviso: Both are premises lent to us, not warehouses with opening hours. Write before you go and we will confirm someone is there to receive you — so you do not load the car only to find the door shut.
cv.lead: If your home was affected by the earthquake, upload a few photos. A volunteer engineer tells you whether there are signs not to stay in it, what precautions to take, and which materials to repair it with.
cv.aviso: This does not replace a visit or your municipality's declaration. What an engineer gives you is an opinion formed at a distance, from your photos: whether there are signs not to stay in the house or in part of it, what precautions to take in the meantime, and which materials to repair it with and in what order. In an emergency that is what can be given quickly, and giving nothing is worse.
cv.gestion: We will try to arrange help for every home we can, and we cannot commit to it house by house. We would rather tell you that up front than promise something that does not depend on us alone.
cv.s1.0: If the danger is happening NOW — a wall about to fall, a smell of gas, someone trapped — this is not what you need: call 123 and your local council. An opinion based on photos has no deadline, and an emergency does not wait.
cv.s1.1: Do not go in if you see collapsed walls, sunken roofs or broken columns. Take the photos from outside.
cv.s1.2: Do not climb onto the roof or onto ladders.
cv.s1.3: Do not move rubble to show the damage better.
cv.s1.4: If you smell gas, get out and tell someone. Do not switch anything on.
cv.s1.5: If there are aftershocks, wait. The house will still be there.
cv.s1.fin: Better one photo less than an accident. If something feels unsafe, skip it and just tell us.
cv.tel.h: We use it to reach you if we need more photos or to arrange a visit.
cv.sector.h: For example: Cali, comuna 18. This is the only part that could ever be made public.

cv.s3.h: Your photos are sent at the end, when you tap “Send my case”. As long as you get that far without closing the page, nothing is lost.

cv.ing.link: Are you an engineer or architect who wants to review cases?
ing.t: There are more damaged homes than engineers to visit them.
ing.lead: After the 10 August earthquake, more requests arrive than any field team can handle. We are not asking you to rule from a distance: we are asking you to look at some photos, say whether there are signs not to stay, and what should be repaired and with what.
ing.q.p: This distinction is not fine print: it governs the whole project, down to the names of the database columns. If you do not share it, this is not the place — and we would rather say so up front.
ing.q1.p: You give an opinion at a distance: whether there are signs not to stay in the house or in part of it, what precautions to take in the meantime, and which materials to repair it with and in what order. And you order the queue: urgent visit, scheduled, none needed for now, or cannot be assessed with this material.
ing.q2.p: You do not declare a home habitable or uninhabitable, and nobody here will ask you to sign that: declarations with legal effects — evacuate, demolish — belong to the municipal authority under Colombia's Law 1523 of 2012. Recommending that part of a house not be used while it is being checked is not declaring it uninhabitable: it is a precaution, and it is written as one.
ing.q3.p: You cannot see the foundation, you cannot see the soil, and you do not know whether that wall is load-bearing. That is why «I cannot assess this» is a first-class answer and not a failure: choosing it forces the system to ask you what is missing, and to request it from the family.
ing.c.t: From application to your first case
ing.p1.p: With your name, your professional licence number and your city. Two minutes.
ing.p2.p: We look it up in COPNIA's public register. A person does this, so it is not instant: it is the only filter the project has and we do not want it automated.
ing.p3.p: With your email address, whichever you prefer — university, company or personal. No account and no password: you request a code, it arrives in your inbox, and you are in.
ing.p4.p: You open a case, see its photos and classify it. You do not see the family's name, phone or address: prioritising by urgency does not require them, and the people who do need them to go and visit are the field team.
ing.f.p: The family receives a PDF with your name, your licence number and what you wrote. That is why you review the cases you want and none that you do not, and why asking for more material is always an option. Nothing about this is charged, in either direction.
ing.form.lead: There is no minimum number of cases and no schedule. There is a verification before you start.
ing.email.h: You would sign in with this same address. University, company or personal — it does not matter.
ing.matricula.h: The one on your COPNIA card. It is what we will verify in their public register.
ing.disp: How many cases could you look at per week (optional)
ing.disp.ph: Two or three, five, whatever comes in…
ing.msg: Anything you would like to tell us? (optional)
ing.msg.ph: Experience in post-earthquake assessment, where you are based, any questions.
ing.alcance: I understand that I am giving an opinion at a distance — staying, precautions, materials and visit priority — and that it is NOT a habitability ruling: that declaration belongs to the municipal authority. Recommending that part of the house not be used while it is being checked is a precaution, not a declaration.
ing.alcance.h: It is the condition of the project. Declarations with legal effects belong to the municipal authority, and you will never be asked to sign one from a distance.
ing.datos: I authorise Give&Grow to process my data in order to verify my licence and contact me about the triage, under Colombia's Law 1581 of 2012 and its Privacy Policy.
ing.nada: Nothing about this is charged, in either direction.

ap.lead: There are families who already have an engineer's written opinion and know what their home needs: roof sheets, a propped wall, cement, a door. What is missing is the means. Here you register what you can contribute and someone from the team writes to you.
ap.no.1.t: You do not pick the home
ap.no.1.p: Which homes are attended is ordered by the engineers' written opinions. Need has an order and a photograph is not that order: letting people choose would put the most photogenic home first, not the most urgent one.
ap.no.2.p: Neither the engineer's opinion nor a repair declares that a home can be lived in. That ruling, with effects such as evacuating or demolishing, belongs to the municipal authority under Colombia's Law 1523 of 2012.
ap.no.3.p: This form asks for no payment details and charges nothing. It records what you offer and a person from the team contacts you to agree on the details.
ap.ev.p: Every delivery we make is published with its record: what was delivered, where, and with which local organisation. We do not promise a home with your name on it; we publish what was actually done.
ap.form.t: Tell us what you can contribute
ap.form.lead: There is no minimum. One bag of cement helps, and so does a company donating thirty.
ap.org: Name of the company or organisation
ap.detalle.ph: Zinc roof sheets, cement, a crew of two bricklayers for a Saturday, a truck heading to Quindío.
ap.detalle.h: Be specific if you can. That is what lets us match it against what the engineers wrote is missing.
ap.alcance.ph: Twenty bags, once a month, available from September.
ap.sector: Territory, if you have a preference
ap.sector.h: We take it into account, but it is not a commitment: priority is still ordered by the engineers' written opinions.
ap.concepto: I understand that sponsoring does NOT reserve a particular home, and that Give&Grow decides which homes are attended using the engineers' written opinions.
ap.concepto.h: It is the project's condition, and it is here so there is no misunderstanding later. If what you want is to support a home you already know, write to us and we will talk it through.
ap.datos: I authorise the processing of my data so that Give&Grow can contact me about this offer, under Colombia's Law 1581 of 2012 and its Privacy Policy.
